title: Q4 Staged Fallbacks, Autoscale Telemetry, and Rollout Matrix for Dedicated Pools
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a Q4 playbook to introduce staged fallbacks for Dedicated capacity and to roll out enhanced autoscale telemetry. The goal is to improve customer-visible availability during capacity pressure while keeping unit cost predictable. This ticket scopes the experiments, telemetry schema, canary/rollout matrix, and a verification checklist for safe production launch.
acceptance_criteria: Staged fallback policy documented and codified (tier definitions, triggers, and rollback conditions)
Autoscale telemetry implemented and feeding a Grafana dashboard with per-pool heatmaps and cost delta metrics
Canary rollout matrix with pass/fail criteria defined and one dry-run canary executed in non-prod
Runbook and rollback playbook published in Confluence and linked from Console rollout UI
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with Eng, SRE, and Console owners. Agreed on 3-tier fallback model: (1) prefix-KV cache warm, (2) quantized model fallbacks, (3) region-level reroute to burst pool.
2025-02-21: Spike complete. ENG spike PR #5482 demonstrates graceful KV cache reuse under eviction; initial perf hit ~+12% CPU but token throughput preserved.

2025-03-03: Telemetry schema v0.1 landed in ENG-9201. New metrics: pool_warm_ratio, fallback_activation_count, per-request_cost_delta, tail_latency_p99_rolling. Grafana draft dashboard created (grafana.redwood.internal/d/auto-autoscale).
2025-03-10: Canary plan drafted. Canary phases: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% traffic slices over 24h windows with MTTD < 10m and rollback if p99 latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.
2025-03-14: Dry-run executed in staging for phase 0.5%. Observed fallback_activation_count spike in pool us-east-1, investigation points to prewarm tuning (ENG task created ENG-9467).
decisions: Adopt staged fallback model rather than single-tier fallthrough to minimize cost impact.
Telemetry will be emitted at request and pool aggregation levels to support both on-call troubleshooting and long-term economics analysis.
Canary windows set to 24h with automated rollback rules enforced by Console release controller.
next_steps: ENG: Implement quantized-model fallback orchestration and validate functional compatibility with function-calling payloads (owner: Priya Nair, ENG-9523)
SRE: Harden prewarm policy tuning script and add synthetic workload tests (owner: Marco Ruiz, ENG-9467)
Console: Add rollout UI flags for staged fallbacks and present rollback button with reason codes (owner: Elaine Park)
PM: Finalize customer communication template and support runbook; coordinate with Solutions for pilot customers
risks: Undetected regression in model output quality when falling back to quantized variants (mitigation: sample-based quality checks and evals tied to canary)
Telemetry volume increase may affect observability costs and dashboard cardinality (mitigation: rollup rules and 7d retention for high-card metrics)
Race conditions during fast rollback could leave requests routed to half-configured pools (mitigation: atomic release controller and preflight checks)
Customer confusion about degraded modes if not communicated clearly (mitigation: UI status banners and API headers indicating fallback reason)
reviewer_feedback: 2025-03-05 (SRE lead - Marco): Suggest moving p99 threshold logic to a sliding-window baseline to avoid transient spikes triggering rollback.
2025-03-12 (Research - Lina Gomez): Add an output-quality regression alert configured on golden prompt set; fallback should not trigger without quality checks passing.
2025-03-16 (Legal): No additional privacy concerns for telemetry as currently scoped; ensure KMS keys used for any exported logs in customer-owned deployments.
